cycle.label: Triennial period
cycle.note: Each permit's triennial reporting period runs January 1 to December 31 three years later.

requirements.label: Total hours each year
requirements.note: At least 20 credits by December 31 each year — $10 fine per missing credit.

requirements.label: Accounting, auditing & attest
requirements.note: 24 credits in accounting, auditing or attestation standards each three-year period if you perform accounting, auditing, assurance or attestation engagements, or prepare or sign any financial report (OAC 4701-15-11(A)).

requirements.label: Taxation
requirements.note: 24 credits in taxation each three-year period if you do tax work on any engagement, or prepare or sign any tax return (OAC 4701-15-11(B)).

requirements.label: Professional Standards & Responsibilities (Ohio)
requirements.note: 3 credits each three-year period from a course approved by the Board as Professional Standards and Responsibilities — it can cover Ohio accountancy law and rules, professional ethics, ethical philosophy, or another state's accountancy laws. We count courses with "PSR", "Professional Standards and Responsibilities", or "Ohio" and "ethics" in the title — edit the title if your approved course isn't picked up.

newLicensee.note: Initial period: 40 credits from January 1 of the year you were certified through December 31 of the next year — no yearly minimum or subject requirements.

licenseDateHint: Ohio reporting periods end December 31 (e.g. 12/31/2027). New licensees: Dec 31 of the year after you were certified.
issueDateHint: The date on your CPA certificate — sets your initial two-year period.
limitsNotTracked: Live group study: max 8 credits in one day.
Professional exams: max 40 credits per session; election official service: max 20 per period.
toVerify: Reporting period timing is per permit; the user enters their period end (Dec 31). New-licensee initial period detected when that end is Dec 31 of the year after the certificate year.
PSR course recognised by title keywords; the Board approves specific Ohio courses.
PSR courses are Board-approved individually; title matching ('PSR', 'Professional Standards and Responsibilities', 'Ohio'+'ethics') may miss an approved course with another title.
